title: What Percentage Is a 5 in IB? Grade Guide
summary: What percentage is a 5 in IB? Learn why it varies by subject, level, session, and component, then check the exact boundary for your IB course.
body_markdown:
A 5 in IB does **not correspond to one universal percentage** . As a rough planning estimate, scores around **50-65%** may fall within grade 5 territory in many subjects, but the actual threshold can sit outside that range. It depends on the subject, Standard Level or Higher Level, assessment component, exam session, and sometimes timezone.


The only reliable conversion is the boundary for your exact course and session. RevisionDojo's[IB Grade Boundaries tool](https://www.revisiondojo.com/grade-boundaries) lets you select those details and see the relevant conversion.


That is the direct answer. But understanding why the answer moves is what prevents a percentage from creating either false confidence or unnecessary panic.


### The short answer at a glance


- There is no fixed percentage that always equals an IB 5.
- A rough estimate is often around 50-65%, with meaningful exceptions.
- Boundaries differ by subject, level, session, component, and sometimes timezone.
- A grade boundary is the minimum mark required for a particular grade.
- Your final subject grade combines weighted assessment components rather than treating every raw mark equally.
- For an exact answer, use the boundary published for your course and session.


### Why an IB 5 is not a fixed percentage


Imagine a student opening a marked practice test and seeing 62%. The number feels complete. It is precise enough to invite an immediate conclusion: surely that must be a 5.


But 62% is only the beginning of the calculation. The student still needs to ask what subject the test covered, whether it was SL or HL, which component it represented, and which examination session provides the comparison. Without that context, the percentage is like a temperature without a scale.


The IB awards subject grades on a **1-7 scale** . Raw and weighted marks are converted into those grades using boundaries established for the relevant assessment session. According to the IB's assessment guidance, boundary setting involves reviewing the quality of student work against grade descriptors. This helps explain why a threshold is not simply chosen as a permanent percentage in advance.


The[RevisionDojo guide to how IB grade boundaries affect final scores](https://www.revisiondojo.com/blog/ib-grade-boundaries-affect-final-score) explores how the same percentage can lead to different outcomes when the context changes.


A student asks an information clerk where a 62 percent mark belongs while signs point toward subject, level, and session


### How IB grade boundaries convert marks into grades


A boundary is the lowest mark needed to earn a particular grade. Consider a hypothetical boundary table:


Weighted percentage Illustrative IB grade


70-100% 7


60-69% 6


50-59% 5


40-49% 4


In this illustration, 50% is the lower boundary for a 5. A student receiving 58% would also earn a 5, while 60% would reach a 6.


These figures are **illustrative only** . They are not official boundaries for every subject or session. Actual[IB grade boundaries explained for parents](https://www.revisiondojo.com/blog/ib-grade-boundaries-explained-parent-guide) can shift, which is why a generic conversion chart should never replace the course-specific data.


There is another important detail. Your overall percentage may be weighted rather than calculated as a simple average. If one assessment component contributes more heavily to the final subject result, it has a greater effect on the final weighted mark.


A simplified calculation might look like this:

This is why averaging the percentages printed on several pieces of work can produce a misleading prediction.


### A dated example of what variation looks like


A clearly dated example makes the problem easier to see. RevisionDojo's archived **2025 IB Digital Society HL** table lists the grade 5 interval as **51-61** , followed by a grade 6 interval of 62-71. That example applies to the subject, level, and session represented by the table. It should not be transferred to Biology, Mathematics, English, or another year.


The broader lesson is more useful than the particular numbers. A mark becomes meaningful only after it is paired with the correct boundary. Students comparing Mathematics results can begin with the dedicated[IB Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches boundaries](https://www.revisiondojo.com/grade-boundaries/ib-math-aa) , while families wanting historical context can read the[2025 guide to understanding IB grade boundaries](https://www.revisiondojo.com/blog/understanding-ib-grade-boundaries-2025-what-they-mean-and-how-to-use-them) .


### Is a 5 a good IB grade?


A 5 represents solid performance on the IB's 1-7 scale. Its practical meaning, however, depends on what the student needs it to do.


For one student, a 5 may satisfy a course condition and provide a comfortable foundation. For another, particularly someone facing a subject-specific university requirement, the goal may need to be a 6 or 7. Parents should therefore avoid treating the number as either universally strong or universally disappointing.


The more useful questions are:


- Is the 5 consistent or close to a boundary?
- Which components are limiting the weighted total?
- What grade does the student's university offer require?
- Is improvement most likely to come from knowledge, technique, timing, or written communication?


A student two marks below a 6 faces a different task from one who has only just reached a 5. The label is the same, but the revision strategy should not be.


### How to use a percentage without being misled


Begin by matching the mark to the correct subject, level, and session in the[RevisionDojo Grade Boundaries feature](https://www.revisiondojo.com/features/grade-boundaries) . Then check whether the percentage represents one component or a weighted overall result.


Next, use the boundary diagnostically. If the mark is close to a 6, look for a small number of repeatable improvements. These might include showing complete working, using command terms accurately, supporting analysis with evidence, or leaving enough time to answer the final question.


If the mark is near the bottom of the grade 5 interval, return to foundational gaps before chasing marginal examination tricks. RevisionDojo's **Questionbank** can isolate weak topics, while **Study Notes** and **Flashcards** help rebuild knowledge. **AI Chat** can clarify difficult ideas, and **Grading tools** can provide structured feedback on responses.


Once those gaps narrow, **Predicted Papers** and **Mock Exams** help students practise complete assessments under timed conditions. The **Coursework Library** provides useful models for understanding structure, and experienced **Tutors** can help when a student needs individual guidance. Together, these tools make RevisionDojo the ultimate IB resource for moving from a grade estimate to a practical improvement plan.


### What students and parents should remember


The student looking at 62% wanted the number to deliver certainty. What it really delivered was a better question.


Do not ask only, “Is 62% a 5?” Ask, “Is 62% a 5 for this subject, at this level, in this session, after the correct weighting?” That small change replaces guesswork with context.


For the precise conversion, enter your course details in RevisionDojo's[Grade Boundaries tool](https://www.revisiondojo.com/grade-boundaries) . It is the quickest way to find the exact threshold relevant to your result and decide what to work on next.
